accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding rights read into Article 21 by the Supreme Court:

List-I (Right)
a. Fair, just and reasonable procedure
b. Right to live with human dignity
c. Right to speedy trial
d. Right to free legal aid

List-II (Case)
i. Hussainara Khatoon
ii. M.H. Hoskot
iii. Maneka Gandhi
aiv. Francis Coralie Mullin

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Maneka Gandhi recognised fair, just and reasonable procedure; Francis Coralie Mullin recognised the right to live with human dignity; Hussainara Khatoon concerned speedy trial; and M.H. Hoskot concerned free legal aid.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure case-right pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped pair.
accepted.sec: Human rights read into Article 21 by courts → case

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar (1991) recognised the right to a clean environment. Privacy was recognised in K.S. Puttaswamy, compensation in Nilabati Behera, and speedy trial in Hussainara Khatoon.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related Article 21 rights and their landmark cases.
accepted.sec: Human rights read into Article 21 by courts → case

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding rights read into Article 21:
1. The right to privacy was recognised in K.S. Puttaswamy (2017).
2. Compensation for violation of human rights was associated with Nilabati Behera (1993).
3. The right to die was declared an unrestricted fundamental right in Gian Kaur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: Gian Kaur recognised no general right to death, but accepted the idea of dying with dignity in the constitutionally recognised context.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses the precise distinction between a right to death and a right to die with dignity.
accepted.sec: Human rights read into Article 21 by courts → case

accepted.s:
Arrange the following cases in chronological order:
A. K.S. Puttaswamy
B. Hussainara Khatoon
C. Olga Tellis
D. Subhash Kumar
accepted.x: The relevant years are Hussainara Khatoon (1979), Olga Tellis (1985), Subhash Kumar (1991) and K.S. Puttaswamy (2017).
accepted.tq: Place the earliest and latest cases first, then order the middle cases by year.
accepted.sec: Human rights read into Article 21 by courts → case

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 73 extends the executive power of the Union.
2. Article 51(c) directs the State to foster respect for international law and treaty obligations.
3. Article 253 permits only the executive and not Parliament to implement international treaties through domestic law.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Article 253 specifically empowers Parliament to legislate for implementing treaties and international agreements.
accepted.tq: Identify the wrong authority in the treaty-implementation statement and separate executive power from legislative power.
accepted.sec: International covenants and Indian law - Articles for treaty implementation, CEDAW cases

accepted.s: India has been a party to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) since:
accepted.x: India has been a party to the ICCPR since 1979.
accepted.tq: Use the year-specific international-law fact and reject nearby treaty-related dates.
accepted.sec: International covenants and Indian law - Articles for treaty implementation, CEDAW cases

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India's position regarding the First Optional Protocol to the ICCPR?
o: India has not signed it, so the UN individual-complaint mechanism does not apply to India through that Protocol.
India signed and ratified it in 1979, accepting compulsory individual complaints.
India signed it in 2007 through the establishment of the NCPCR.
India acceded to it in 1992 along with the UNCRC.
accepted.x: India is party to the ICCPR but has not signed its First Optional Protocol, which provides the UN individual-complaint mechanism.
accepted.tq: Separate membership of the main covenant from acceptance of its optional individual-complaint mechanism.
accepted.sec: International covenants and Indian law - Articles for treaty implementation, CEDAW cases

accepted.s: The Vishaka guidelines on workplace sexual harassment were framed by relying substantially on:
o: The First Optional Protocol to the ICCPR
accepted.x: In Vishaka (1997), the Supreme Court relied on the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) to frame workplace-harassment guidelines.
accepted.tq: Match the landmark Indian case with the specific international convention it used.
accepted.sec: International covenants and Indian law - Articles for treaty implementation, CEDAW cases

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding international conventions and Indian courts is correct?
o: Guruvayur Devaswom held that international conventions can never be considered by Indian courts.
Article 51(c) automatically gives every international convention the force of a constitutional amendment.
Vishaka (1997) relied exclusively on the ICCPR and not on CEDAW.
The principles of public interest litigation enabled courts to rely on international conventions in Guruvayur Devaswom (2003).
accepted.x: The principles associated with public interest litigation enabled courts to rely on international conventions in Guruvayur Devaswom (2003). The other statements overstate or misidentify the legal effect and applicable convention.
accepted.tq: Choose the precise judicial use of international conventions rather than an absolute claim about their legal status.
accepted.sec: International covenants and Indian law - Articles for treaty implementation, CEDAW cases

accepted.s: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR), set up in 2007, works in line with which international instrument?
accepted.x: The NCPCR was set up in 2007 and works in line with the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC).
accepted.tq: Link the national child-rights institution with the correct international child-rights instrument.
accepted.sec: International covenants and Indian law - Articles for treaty implementation, CEDAW cases

accepted.s: The Supreme Court's observation that a person does not become a “non-person” after going to jail primarily affirms that:
o: Prisoners lose all constitutional protections during imprisonment.
Prisoners retain human rights subject to lawful restrictions.
Prison authorities may suspend every fundamental right without review.
Only foreign prisoners retain rights in Indian prisons.
accepted.x: Imprisonment does not erase a person's human rights; restrictions must have a lawful basis and prison administration remains subject to constitutional scrutiny.
accepted.tq: Apply the constitutional principle to a prisoner-rights scenario and reject absolute claims.
accepted.sec: Human rights of specific groups - prisoners, manual scavengers, bonded labour

accepted.s: The arrest safeguards laid down in D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal relate primarily to:
o: Recognition of the right to livelihood
Protection of persons during arrest and custodial detention
accepted.x: D.K. Basu (1997) laid down safeguards intended to prevent custodial abuse and protect persons during arrest and detention.
accepted.tq: Associate the case with its precise subject instead of the broader category of human-rights litigation.
accepted.sec: Human rights of specific groups - prisoners, manual scavengers, bonded labour

accepted.s: Which activity is prohibited under the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013?
o: Construction of sanitary latrines by trained workers with protective gear
Providing rehabilitation assistance to identified manual scavengers
Surveying households to identify insanitary latrines
Cleaning insanitary latrines, sewers or septic tanks without protective gear
accepted.x: The 2013 Act bans employment involving cleaning insanitary latrines, sewers and septic tanks without protective gear. Survey and rehabilitation are statutory responses, not prohibited activities.
accepted.tq: Identify the prohibited conduct while separating it from statutory survey, construction and rehabilitation duties.
accepted.sec: Human rights of specific groups - prisoners, manual scavengers, bonded labour

accepted.s: Under the 2013 law relating to manual scavengers, local bodies are required to survey and build sanitary latrines within:
accepted.x: Local bodies are required to conduct surveys and build sanitary latrines within three years under the stated framework.
accepted.tq: Focus on the statutory time period and distinguish it from nearby administrative deadlines.
accepted.sec: Human rights of specific groups - prisoners, manual scavengers, bonded labour

accepted.s: Bonded labour is constitutionally prohibited under:
accepted.x: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings, begar and other similar forms of forced labour, including bonded labour.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the constitutional prohibition of forced labour from neighbouring Articles concerning life, child labour and remedies.
accepted.sec: Human rights of specific groups - prisoners, manual scavengers, bonded labour

accepted.s: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act was enacted in:
accepted.x: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act was enacted in 1976.
accepted.tq: Match the abolition statute with its year and avoid confusing it with later human-rights legislation.
accepted.sec: Human rights of specific groups - prisoners, manual scavengers, bonded labour

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the legal position of transgender persons under the Amendment Act, 2026:
1. Self-perceived identity is excluded under the stated amendment.
2. The District Magistrate issues the certificate.
3. The certificate is issued on the recommendation of a medical board.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct under the stated 2026 amendment: self-perceived identity is excluded, and the District Magistrate issues the certificate on a medical board's recommendation.
accepted.tq: Check each institutional and procedural element rather than assuming the certificate is self-issued.
accepted.sec: Human rights of specific groups - prisoners, manual scavengers, bonded labour

accepted.s: The Global Alliance for Human Rights of the UN Human Rights Office seeks progress before which milestone?
o: The 80th anniversary of the UDHR in December 2028
The 100th anniversary of the UN in 2045
The 75th anniversary of the UDHR in December 2023
The 50th anniversary of the ICCPR in 2016
accepted.x: The Global Alliance for Human Rights targets progress before the 80th anniversary of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in December 2028.
accepted.tq: Use both the anniversary number and the month-year milestone to avoid a familiar-year trap.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: In relation to the alleged custodial death of Gade Sai Krishna, which authorities were reported to have been asked for reports?
o: The Supreme Court, Parliament and CAG
The Union Home Secretary, Election Commission and NCPCR
The Andhra Pradesh Governor, Speaker and Advocate General only
The Andhra Pradesh DGP, Chief Secretary and State Human Rights Commission
accepted.x: Reports were sought from the Andhra Pradesh Director General of Police, Chief Secretary and State Human Rights Commission in relation to the alleged custodial death.
accepted.tq: Identify the authorities by separating the State-level reporting chain from unrelated constitutional bodies.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes a criticism or debate concerning India's human-rights framework?
o: India is not party to the ICCPR, and NHRC has no advisory role.
India has accepted the ICCPR individual-complaint mechanism, and NHRC advice automatically binds all courts.
India has withdrawn from the UNCRC, and NHRC advice can amend legislation directly.
India remains outside the ICCPR individual-complaint mechanism, and NHRC advice is non-binding.
accepted.x: India has not accepted the ICCPR individual-complaint mechanism through the First Optional Protocol, and advice of the NHRC is non-binding.
accepted.tq: Separate two distinct criticisms and reject absolute claims about treaty membership and NHRC powers.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following is regarded as the first human-rights document?
accepted.x: The Magna Carta of 1215 is regarded as the first human-rights document among the listed instruments.
accepted.tq: Apply the first-in-time rule and distinguish the historic document from modern UN covenants and conventions.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Arrange the following instruments in chronological order:
A. CEDAW
B. Magna Carta
C. Universal Declaration of Human Rights
D. ICCPR
accepted.x: The chronological order is Magna Carta (1215), UDHR (1948), ICCPR (1966) and CEDAW (1979).
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the medieval Magna Carta and the latest convention, then place the UN instruments by year.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
